'''Robert Tate''' (born October 19, 1973) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] and [[return specialist]] for nine seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected in the sixth round of the [[1997 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1997 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1997/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-29 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Tate played in the NFL with the [[Minnesota Vikings]], [[Baltimore Ravens]] and [[Arizona Cardinals]]. Tate played [[college football]] for the [[Cincinnati Bearcats football|Cincinnati Bearcats]]. Originally a [[wide receiver]], he was converted to defensive back upon entering the NFL. Tate played at Cincinnati with notable NFL players [[Artrell Hawkins]], [[Sam Garnes]], and [[Jason Fabini]].

'''Robert Pollard''' (born June 28, 1981) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Pollard played [[college football]] for the [[TCU Horned Frogs football|TCU Horned Frogs]] on a football scholarship and graduated [[Texas Christian University]] with a Bachelor of Science degree in psychology in 2003.<ref>{{cite news|via=newspapers.com|accessdate=2023-05-11|newspaper=Fort Worth Star-Telegram|author=Pierce, Damien|title=Quarterback often place where TCU's ends meet|date=December 19, 2003|page=10D|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/fort-worth-star-telegram/124411933/}}</ref> Afterward, he signed with the [[San Diego Chargers]] as a free agent (2004), then the [[Seattle Seahawks]] (2005–2006) of the [[National Football League]] before injuring his knee, ending his NFL career. After spending 2007 recovering from the injury, Pollard signed with the [[Dallas Desparados]] of the [[Arena Football League (2008)|Arena Football League]] and played for a year before the entire arena football league was put on hiatus the following year.

His father [[Bob Pollard]] played 154 games in the NFL as a defensive lineman.<ref>{{cite web|title=Robert Pollard|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PollBo20.htm|publisher=Sports Reference|work=Pro Football Reference|accessdate=2023-05-11}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|via=newspapers.com|accessdate=2023-05-11|newspaper=Fort Worth Star-Telegram|author=Myers, Tracey|title=Like father, like son|date=October 11, 2002|page=12D|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/fort-worth-star-telegram/124411933/}}</ref> Pollard now works as a peace officer in Texas.
